mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of episodes where FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincides with weakening household demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and compresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 4% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly different from zero during periods of sustained sub-4% unemployment.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months indicates weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of episodes where INDPRO is below its 12-month MA for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the federal funds rate and a decline in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) over a two-month period signals a disinflationary tightening, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises AND CPIAUCSL falls over two months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower during periods of simultaneous FEDFUNDS increases and CPIAUCSL declines.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated increase in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) above their respective 12-month moving averages for two consecutive months signals a robust demand recovery, which boosts earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > 12-month MA AND HOUST > 12-month MA for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher during coordinated GDPC1 and HOUST expansions above their 12-month moving averages.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months signals strengthening labor demand, which supports corporate revenue growth and justifies higher equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during periods of sustained above-trend payroll employment growth.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive relationship exists between real retail sales (RSAFS) growth and S&P 500 forward returns at the 5-day horizon: higher-than-expected monthly RSAFS growth is associated with higher near-term equity returns, regardless of macro regime.
failure_condition: The correlation between monthly RSAFS growth and subsequent 5-day S&P 500 returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.10) over any 5-year rolling window.
